walkthroughs.body_html:
Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons.

Fractional distillation: heated, vapours rise; cooler at top.

Short chains (gases) at top; long chains (bitumen) at bottom.
Bigger molecules: higher bp, more viscous, less flammable.

Today: 78% N2, 21% O2, ~1% Ar, ~0.04% CO2.

Early atmosphere: mostly CO2 from volcanoes.

mcqs.q: When water boils, what is broken?
options: The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.
Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
